sentences.text: Dracoraptor is a genus of coelophysoid dinosaur whose name translates to "dragon thief".
This animal was a bipedal dinosaur, walking on two legs like its relatives.
The construction of its pelvis indicates that Dracoraptor belonged to the saurischian group of dinosaurs.
Its skull featured transversely flattened, dagger-shaped teeth with serrated edges, a trait found only in theropods.
In 2016, researchers identified eighteen distinguishing traits, known as autapomorphies, that set this species apart.
A furcula, or wishbone, was present in the fossil, a feature that is rarely seen in early theropod dinosaurs.
The pubic bone in the pelvis measured 212 millimeters in length.
Dracoraptor holds the distinction of being the oldest dinosaur discovered in Wales.
This specimen represents the most complete Mesozoic theropod ever found in Wales.
To date, only one fossil occurrence of Dracoraptor has been recorded in scientific databases.
Fossils were first discovered in 2014 in the Blue Lias Formation on the coast of South Wales, near the village of Penarth.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as NMW 2015.5G.1–2015.5G.11, was found in the lower Bull Cliff Member of the Blue Lias Formation.
The species Dracoraptor hanigani was formally named and described in 2016 by David Martill, Steven Vidovic, Cindy Howells, and John Nudds.
Dracoraptor was a meat-eater that likely fed on small vertebrate animals, indicated by its small, about one-centimeter-long, pointed and serrated teeth.
Due to its small size and long legs, Dracoraptor was likely capable of running at high speeds.
Based on limited ecological data, researchers in 2016 tentatively illustrated Dracoraptor as a shore-dwelling predator and scavenger.
Dracoraptor is considered the most basal member of the Coelophysoidea group.
A 2016 cladistic analysis determined Dracoraptor was a basal member of Neotheropoda, near the base of the evolutionary tree.
The genus belongs to the parent group Coelophysoidea and is classified within the class Reptilia.
Dracoraptor lived during the Hettangian stage of the Early Jurassic, approximately 201 million years ago, in what is now Wales.
The holotype is precisely dated to 201.3 million years ago, based on its precise geological layer.
This precise dating places the specimen at 201.3 million years ago, with a margin of error of ±0.2 million years.
